title: Swann's Way (Du cote de chez Swann)

access.edition_or_version: First edition, Bernard Grasset, Paris, November 1913; English trans. C. K. Scott-Moncrieff (Project Gutenberg #7178); French original #2650

mechanics.premise: A sleeping narrator tastes an old pastry in tea and the texture of a vanished childhood quarter of Paris returns; interwoven, Swann's love affair is narrated largely through recollection and reinterpretation of the past.
mechanics.point_of_view: First-person retrospective narrator (the adult looking back), with long embedded focalization onto Swann.
mechanics.psychic_distance: Distance closes abruptly through sensory detail in the involuntary-memory episode and opens again into retrospective commentary - the oscillation itself carries the tone.
mechanics.style_and_devices: Long periodic sentences grounding abstraction in sensory objects; recursive temporal markers; scenes built from domestic things (rooms, streets, a cup of tea); the sentence enacts the return of time rather than naming it.
mechanics.emotional_progression: Dormancy - sensory trigger - flooded return - reflective integration; in the Swann line, infatuation - habit - loss - compulsive re-collected longing.
mechanics.dialogue: Dialogue mostly framed by narrated memory rather than present-tense exchange, keeping the reader inside recollection.
mechanics.conventions: Belletrist novel of memory using the childhood-rooms frame common to memoir.
mechanics.innovation_or_subversion: Makes the mechanics of remembering itself the subject: memory is unreliable, selective, and world-creating rather than a record.
mechanics.critical_reception: Foundational text of twentieth-century fiction; the sensory-trigger episode is the standard literary reference point for involuntary memory.
mechanics.audience_reception: Frequently cited by readers and writers as the definitive experience of being pulled bodily into the past.
